title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered, Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used the declared generator gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 within the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes used in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.74468085%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. We reconcile preregistration natural-language hypothesis wording with the registered formal estimand, document per-condition pipeline semantics with artifact references (execution/model_configuration.json, execution/execution_manifest.json, analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json), disclose a protocol deviation (unset runtime sampling temperature in execution/model_configuration.json), and discuss operational interpretation and limitations constrained by synthetic scope and single-model/validator evaluation. All principal numeric claims are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in Methods and Results.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as productivity tools for network operations (NetOps): translating operator intent into device CLI, synthesizing multi-step workflows, and aiding change planning. However, using LLM outputs directly in operational pipelines risks syntax and semantic errors, unsafe ordering of commands, and adversarially-induced unsafe outputs. Prior prototype studies indicate that coupling LLM generation with deterministic verification and localized repair improves draft quality, but prior evaluations often use token- or reference-match metrics that do not measure deployability or acceptance-for-deployment.

This study asks a focused, operational research question that we preregistered before execution: How effective are template-based input sanitization and deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? The design intentionally operationalizes the estimand as validator acceptance-for-deployment (a binary outcome determined by deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and uses paired shared_initial_candidate semantics so that post-generation defenses (sanitization, gating, repair) are the only source of paired differences. The preregistered plan, execution artifacts, and analysis are archived; key artifact references appear throughout Methods and Results.
sections.related_work:
Deterministic network-verification tools such as Header Space Analysis and VeriFlow provide formal checks of forwarding and configuration invariants and have been used as validators in LLM-assisted NetOps pipelines [1,2]. Empirical work on LLMs for network configuration reports that models produce useful drafts but commonly commit syntax/ordering errors; coupling generation with verifier feedback and localized repair yields prototype improvements in deployable outputs [3,4]. Surveys of AIOps and telecom LLM applications call for evaluation metrics that measure operational safety and deployability rather than lexical accuracy [5,6]. Security analyses of LLM-integrated systems demonstrate prompt-injection and indirect-prompt vulnerabilities motivating input-sanitization and gating defenses [7]. Tool-augmented orchestration patterns (LLMs calling external checks and repairing outputs) have conceptual precedent in tool-using LLM research and prior NetOps prototypes [8,3].

Our experiment differs from prior work in three ways: (i) it is preregistered with a single paired formal estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) measured on adversarially mutated intents; (ii) it enforces shared_initial_candidate semantics so that observed paired differences isolate post-generation processing rather than changes to initial generation; and (iii) the run publishes per-episode validator traces and deterministic reconciliation artifacts so each principal number is traceable to archived files (examples: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt; execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json).
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and formal estimand. The study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to observing outcomes (preregistration_sha256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where the binary outcome for each adversarial intent equals 1 if the deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) would accept the final candidate for deployment and 0 otherwise. The confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes; bootstrap percentile 95% CIs use 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729 (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).

Design, task bank and scope. The preregistration specified N = 150 adversarial intents (planned episodes = 300 across two conditions). The synthetic intent templates exercise interface admin changes, MTU and VLAN operations, safe ordering patterns, and constrained required sequences. The adversary model comprises deterministic mutation heuristics applied to templates; generation seeds and mutation taxonomy are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl. Scope is explicitly limited to synthetic templates and the deterministic CLI grammar used by the validator; no private production data was used.

Model, validator, orchestration and declared configuration. The archived run declares the generator as gpt-5-mini and the deterministic validator as deterministic_netops_validator_v5 in execution/model_configuration.json. The orchestration adapter family is hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and the run implemented a generate–validate–repair workflow with template-based input sanitization applied on the guarded branch prior to gating. The archived execution/model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null; we treat the unset temperature as a protocol deviation and report it explicitly in the Disclosure Statement below.

Detailed per-condition pipeline timeline and shared_initial_candidate semantics (artifact-grounded). To address reviewer requests, we describe the exact per-pair call/validation sequence used in the archived execution (execution/execution_manifest.json; analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json):
1) Task instantiation and adversarial mutation are recorded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (e.g., task-000001 payload shows the mutated intent and required_sequence). Sanitizer outcomes (where slots were changed or dropped) are recorded in task_manifest payload fields.
2) Shared initial generation: per pair a single LLM call produced a shared_initial_candidate saved to execution/responses/task-<id>-shared-initial.txt and referenced by both the baseline and guarded scoring artifacts. Evidence: stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 150 in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and per-episode shared_initial_candidate files cited in execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json.
3) Baseline scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 evaluated the shared_initial_candidate and produced validation_before/validation_after traces in execution/scoring/<...>-baseline.json.
4) Guarded branch: template-based input-sanitization was applied prior to gating; if gating allowed the candidate the pipeline permitted at-most-one automated repair LLM call. Repair-stage traces are present where repair occurred; repair stage_counts = 6 in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json. Guarded final decisions and validator traces are stored in execution/scoring/<...>-guarded.json.
5) Final validation: the validator re-evaluated cleaned or repaired candidates and recorded the guarded final decision and validator trace (validation_after). Representative per-episode artifacts include execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json which contain validation_before and validation_after states.
sections.results:
Execution and aggregated counts. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; failed episodes = 18; model provider calls used = 156 (execution/execution_manifest.json). The primary confirmatory analysis used 141 complete pairs (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Condition summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline_successes = 135/141 (0.9574468085) and guarded_successes = 141/141 (1.0). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 135, n10 = 6 (guarded=1, baseline=0), n01 = 0, n00 = 0.

Statistical inference. An exact two-sided McNemar test on the observed paired outcomes yields p = 0.03125. The point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. The 95% bootstrap percentile CI using 10,000 resamples (seed = 1729) is [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]; these parameters and outputs are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv.

Discordant-case diagnostics and repair accounting. The six discordant n10 pairs are fully traceable in the archived artifacts and are associated with permitted repair-stage activity: analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json records repair = 6 and provider-call accounting shows stage_counts.repair = 6. Corresponding scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/task-<id>-guarded.json) contain validator before/after snapshots showing that sanitization and/or the permitted repair altered command ordering or normalization such that deterministic_netops_validator_v5 accepted the final configuration while the unguarded baseline candidate had failed. Representative example: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt with paired scoring artifacts execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json.

Missingness sensitivity. Nine pairs were both-run technical failures and were excluded under the preregistered missingness_plan (analysis/missingness_summary.csv: both_missing_pairs = 9). Under a conservative sensitivity that maps both-missing pairs to failures, baseline acceptance becomes 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance 141/150 = 0.9400. The primary McNemar inference uses only the 141 complete pairs and the observed discordant set (n10 = 6, n01 = 0); the archived paired table reproduces the reported p-value and CI.

Unexecuted preregistered items. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed in the archived run; their absence is documented in execution/execution_manifest.json and the task directories. Consequently, this run provides no empirical false-positive-blocking rates and reports no claims about blocking of benign inputs.
sections.discussion:
Reconciliation of preregistration wording and formal estimand. The preregistration's natural-language H1 stated that verifier-gating would reduce attacker success (fewer unsafe configurations accepted). The registered formal estimand, however, measures paired validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). These constructs can diverge: an increase in validator acceptance can reflect successful repair of otherwise malformed drafts (reducing operator labor) rather than enabling attacker success. Our observed data show guarded > baseline acceptance (≈4.255 percentage points) because sanitizer+repair recovered reparable drafts that the baseline validator rejected. Therefore the preregistered directional wording (attacker-success reduction) is not supported by this formal-estimand outcome; we report and interpret the formal estimand result and explicitly caution against conflating validator acceptance with attacker-centric safety without an independent semantic-safety oracle.

Operational interpretation and repair–gate co-design. Within the controlled synthetic setting, input sanitization plus limited automated repair can recover valid, deployable configurations that unguarded generation fails to produce. Deterministic gating serves as a safety boundary, but its operational effect depends on repair policy and validator coverage. The six discordant cases illustrate a trade-off: repairs enabled acceptance but could—under weaker validator encodings—accept outputs that are semantically unsafe. Thus, operational deployment requires co-design of gating rules, limits on automatic repair, and validators that encode the semantic properties relevant to intended production semantics (beyond CLI grammar and ordering).

Threats to validity. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective sample size and triggered the preregistered exclusion rule (both-run failures = 9). Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 encodes CLI grammar, required sequences, and protected-interface invariants but omits some protocol-level dynamic semantics; acceptance-for-deployment is therefore a partial proxy for operational safety. External validity: single-generator (gpt-5-mini), single-validator, and synthetic intents limit generalization across vendors, protocols, and production traffic. Conclusion validity: the observed absolute effect is small on top of a high baseline acceptance (ceiling effect); statistical detectability does not imply large practical impact.

Recommendations grounded in archival evidence. Based on execution and reconciliation artifacts, immediate next steps are: (1) execute the preregistered benign-control to measure false-positive blocking and the secondary false-positive-blocking estimand; (2) preregister and evaluate an attacker-centric estimand that couples validator acceptance with an independent semantic-safety oracle or operational reachability checks; (3) diversify generator and validator implementations across vendor CLIs and protocol semantics; and (4) fix sampling settings (e.g., temperature = 0) for deterministic reproduction. Each recommendation follows directly from documented artifacts (execution/model_configuration.json; analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference = 0.04255319148936165; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]). Per-episode validator traces and reconciliation stage_counts indicate that the six discordant pairs were associated with permitted repair calls that enabled acceptance. Crucially, this formal-estimand improvement does not equate to measured reduction in attacker-success under attacker-centric definitions. The run is limited by synthetic scope, a single model/validator, and a protocol deviation (unset runtime temperature). Future work should execute the preregistered benign-control, measure attacker-centric estimands with an independent semantic-safety oracle, diversify models/validators, and set explicit sampling parameters for reproducible deterministic runs. All principal numbers and reconciliation claims above are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in Methods and Results (artifact paths cited above and in the Disclosure Statement).

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock under the archived master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; all literature review, preregistration, study selection, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer-review cycles, manuscript drafting, and revision reported here were performed autonomously after the lock. Declared models/tools and orchestration: primary generator = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json), deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration: study cand-2026-03 was preregistered and archived prior to observing outcomes (preregistration_sha256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). Protocol deviation: the archived run recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature (temperature = null in execution/model_configuration.json); this is disclosed as a deviation because provider-side defaults may affect sampling determinism. To preserve paired comparability the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics (single shared generation per pair) and provider-call accounting documented in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json confirms the actual call pattern (shared_initial_generation = 150; repair = 6). Key archived artifact references (examples): execution/task_manifest.jsonl; execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt; execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json; execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json; analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; analysis/condition_summary.csv; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl; execution/model_configuration.json; execution/execution_manifest.json. No human manually edited or corrected the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
